policy.title: Privacy policy
policy.intro: Hoardex is a personal, non-commercial portfolio project that shows the library and playing time of a Steam profile. Signing in is optional and there are no ads. This page explains what data it handles, where it is kept and for how long.

input.heading: What you send and what is shown
input.body: The profile you enter (a URL, a custom name or a SteamID64) goes to Hoardex’s server, which asks Steam’s official Web API for the profile and its game library and returns them. The Steam API key never leaves the server. Hoardex shows what Steam returns for that profile: display name, avatar, games and hours played. It cannot check what each visitor could see on Steam, so enter your own profile, and set it to private on Steam if you do not want it shown.

storage.heading: What Hoardex keeps
storage.body: To avoid asking Steam again and again, Hoardex keeps copies for a short time in a database (Upstash Redis, on AWS in North Virginia, USA):

items.alias: The name you typed and the SteamID it matches: {duration}.
items.profile: The profile: display name, avatar address, profile address, visibility and creation date: {duration}.
items.library: The library: game names, hours played and last-played dates: {duration}.
items.cooldown: After a manual refresh, the SteamID and the time: {refresh} ({retry} if the refresh failed), to limit how often a profile is refreshed.
items.art: If a game’s cover does not load, the addresses of its images in the Steam store: {duration}. They are kept per game, unrelated to any profile.

storage.after: These copies are not kept any longer. Only what you save yourself after signing in lasts longer, as described below. The site’s CDN may also hold an answer for a few minutes.

hosting.heading: Hosting
hosting.body: The site is hosted on Vercel, with its server in the eastern United States. Vercel, like any host, processes technical data such as your IP address to deliver the site, under its own privacy policy. Hoardex does not keep its own logs of visitors.

signIn.heading: Signing in with Steam
signIn.body: Signing in is optional; without it everything works the same. Hoardex sends you to Steam’s own page, and Steam tells Hoardex only your SteamID: Hoardex never sees your password, your email or any data that is not already public. While a sign-in is under way your browser keeps a cookie for at most {login}, and Hoardex’s database keeps the one-time code Steam sent for {login} so it cannot be used twice. Once you are signed in, your browser keeps a cookie with your SteamID, signed by Hoardex, for {session} or until you sign out. Signing in does not make a private Steam library visible.

manual.heading: Your manual states
manual.body: If you sign in, Hoardex keeps an account in its database (Neon Postgres, on AWS in North Virginia, USA): your SteamID and when you first and last signed in. When you set a game’s state by hand, it also keeps the state, when you set it and your playtime for that game at that moment. It also keeps the name and colour of each category you create, the colour you give a built-in one and which built-in categories you deleted. These states and categories are public: anyone who opens your profile sees them, signed in or not. A copy is kept in Upstash Redis for up to {backlog}, renewed with every change. They stay until you return each game to its automatic state, delete each category, or delete your account from your account page, which removes everything at once.

snapshots.heading: Playtime history (optional)
snapshots.body: Only if you turn it on in your account page: once a day, Hoardex asks Steam for your library and saves, for each game whose hours changed since the last time, its total hours and the date, plus since when it is on. It stops if you have not signed in to Hoardex for {days} days, and resumes when you sign in again. Turning it off deletes the whole history.

analytics.heading: Analytics
analytics.body: Vercel Web Analytics counts page views: the address visited (profile name included, but never what you type in a search box or pick in a filter), country, device, browser, operating system and where you came from. It uses no cookies; to tell visitors apart it uses a hash that changes every day. Reports are kept for one month and only the site’s owner can see them.

device.heading: On your device
device.body: Hoardex saves a few things in your browser’s local storage: your language; the SteamID of each profile you refresh with the time its wait of {refresh} ends (removed the next time you refresh); and the states you set in the demo library. They stay on your device. The only cookies are the sign-in ones described above, and only if you sign in.

steam.heading: Steam images
steam.body: Game covers and avatars load directly from Steam’s servers (Valve and its content delivery providers), which therefore receive your IP address and browser details, as with any image. Hoardex asks for them without telling Steam which page you are on.

rights.heading: Your data and how to ask
rights.body: Copies expire on their own within {longest}, most within {profile}. To have a profile’s copies removed sooner, to ask what is kept, or for anything else about your data, write to:
rights.authority: You can also complain to your data protection authority (in Spain, the AEPD).
